releases.notes:
# Sable Mob Interactions 1.1.0

Mobs can now spawn driving custom vehicles. This is the biggest update so far.

## Requirements
- Minecraft 1.21.1 with NeoForge
- Create and Sable
- SableCat 1.0.3 or newer (required)
- Simulated, Create Connected and Offroad (needed by the built-in car)

## What's new

### Mob-driven vehicles
- Vehicles spawn as physics sub-levels with a mob in the driver's seat.
- Pilots drive with the new Mob Transmitter block and can wander, chase and circle players, avoid obstacles and players, and reverse out of jams.
- Pilots respawn if you leave the area or reload the world.
- Cars calibrate their own steering and throttle direction, so most builds drive correctly without setup.
- Each tier has its own max_speed.

### Spawn nodes
- Each tier has a node: a road structure that spawns cars nearby.
- Nodes sit on a levelled pad with tapered edges, so they stay clear of trees and hills.
- The pad matches its surroundings: sandstone and sand in deserts, packed mud, red sand and terracotta in badlands, snow in snowy biomes, gravel and stone on stony shores, and dirt and grass everywhere else.
- Nodes only generate in open biomes (plains, desert, savanna, badlands and similar). The list is a biome tag you can edit: sablemobinteractions:vehicle_node_biomes.
- Nodes follow each tier's ring (min_radius and max_radius), and are skipped on steep terrain and near water.
- Nodes fill with cars much faster than before, and cars are placed only on flat, clear ground and no longer spawn inside each other.
- /place structure now works for nodes. It ignores the biome, ring, flatness and sea level checks, so you can place one anywhere for testing.

### Custom cars
- Put your own .nbt car files in saves/<world>/vehicles/<tier>, for example saves/<world>/vehicles/tier_1_scrap.
- They join that tier's pool and are rescanned as files change.
- The built-in car is copied into the tier 1 folder the first time a world needs it. Delete it from that folder if you don't want it in your pool.
- If a tier's folder is empty, the built-in car is installed again so the tier always has something to spawn.

### New driving goals
- avoid_water: steers away from deep water and lava.
- avoid_cliffs: steers away from large drops.
- slow_turn: slows down before sharp turns so cars are less likely to flip.
- stay_upright: reduces speed when tilted, and rights a car that has flipped over and stopped.
- Chase and wander now interrupt each other properly.

### Commands
- /sablemobinteractions vehicles
- /sablemobinteractions customcars
- /sablemobinteractions clearvehicles
- /sablemobinteractions debugdrive <true|false>

clearvehicles removes only cars spawned by the mod, never vehicles built by players. It needs SableCat.

## Fixed
- Cars driving in a straight line while the wheels wiggle.
- Steering flipping direction on cars that drive with the throttle reversed.
- Pilots that never respawned after leaving the area.
- Cars spawning on cliffs, on tree canopies and inside trees.
- Long waits before a node filled with cars.
- A lot of log spam, which now only appears with debug logging on.

## Upgrading
- Nodes only appear in newly generated chunks. Existing worlds will see them as they explore.
- If you have your own tier JSON files, add the new goals before unstick:
  avoid_water, avoid_cliffs, slow_turn, stay_upright.
- If your tier JSON lists the built-in car under structures, set it to [] so it doesn't get picked twice.
- Custom cars live in each world's vehicles folder. They are not copied between worlds automatically.
- Several old test commands were removed.

releases.notes:
## Sable Mob Interactions v1.0.1

The first release. Hostile mobs, vanilla or modded, can now genuinely see, target, and damage Sable sub-levels: ships, airships, rovers, and anything else built on Sable's sub-level system.

### Highlights

- **Vanilla mobs, properly tuned.** Skeletons fire real arrows, Drowned throw tridents, zombies punch through hulls, creepers explode near your vessel (toggleable), guardians charge a beam, and Endermen make off with your decor (toggleable).
- **Any mod's mobs, automatically.** A generic fallback goal gives any other hostile mob a real target and steps back, letting its own attack AI (melee, ranged, or a fully custom weapon system) fire naturally, with zero code required from that mod's author. Tested against Scorched Guns Neoforged's gunner mobs.
- **Any mod's projectiles, automatically.** Arrows, tridents, bullets, and anything else extending vanilla's Projectile class correctly damage sub-level blocks on impact, regardless of who fired them.
- **Stuck-projectile culling.** Arrows and other projectiles that embed in a sub-level block are automatically cleaned up a short time after impact, rather than persisting indefinitely and adding tracking overhead to a moving sub-level. Normal terrain hits are unaffected.
- **Ship-aware targeting.** Sub-levels only become valid targets if they contain real propulsion/structural parts (a configurable block tag) and have a player nearby, so idle player builds stay safe by default.
- **Optional deep compatibility.** Create: Big Cannons' own block armor system scales how many hits a block takes to break, if installed.
- **Fully configurable.** Search radius, attack range, fire rate, hit thresholds, creeper griefing, Enderman theft, ship-detection strictness, player-presence range, and more, all editable from the in-game config screen.
- **A public API for other modders.** Implement `SubLevelAttacker` on your own mob for tighter, purpose-built control instead of relying on the generic fallback.

### Requires

- [Sable](https://modrinth.com/mod/sable)

Everything else, Create, Create Aeronautics, Create Submarine, Create: Big Cannons, is optional and only enhances specific behaviors when present.
